description.value:
"You do not stop. They learn this the hard way."

Doctrine: Momentum is the point — geography deciding to move.

The Avalanche is mass that arrives all at once. Your Surge spends are forward motion made lethal: barrel through, crash home, and — when it matters — become a thing nothing in the world can currently stop.

Path (spent via Surge)

  • Roll Forward (1) — your next Strike +Tier d6, and the target is knocked Prone.
  • Crash (3) — your next Strike lands as a max-die crit; the target is Staggered.
  • Unstoppable (5) — immune to forced-movement/CC this round; your next Strike ignores resistances and knocks the target Prone.

Tier 2 — Rosicrucian

“I don’t preach Enlightenment. I smuggle it.”

Your network makes progress easier to sustain. People advance faster when the path is lit — and when someone is quietly removing the traps.

Strategic (Faction / Party Scale)

  • When the party earns Enlightenment Points or meets narrative criteria for advancement, increase the rate of progress by 10% (GM adjudicates exact pacing benefits)

This is not a miracle. This is logistics — and Rosicrucians have always been very good at logistics.

Cost: accelerated progress strains the chain supporting it. Expect supply burden, mentor fatigue, increased expectations, or rival attention once advancement starts looking organized instead of accidental.

Automated: Polarity Mastery (melee strike, base die ≥ 8 → +1 Surge 1/round), Anchor or Advance + The Breach (clickable, 1/scene).

"Set your feet. The line forms on you."

The Bulwark is the wall — and the wall runs on Surge, like everyone, but yours arrives the hard way: every time you take Integrity damage you bank +1 Surge (max +2/round). You eat the blow and turn it into the power to anchor, erupt, or hold. At zero Surge you still stand in the way; soak one hit and your turn opens up.

The Fortress (spent via Surge — Bulwark only)

  • Brace Wall (1) — you and adjacent allies gain DR equal to Tier this round.
  • Bulwark Stance (6) — adjacent allies share your defenses until your next turn.
  • Anchor (5) — you and one ally become immune to forced movement and crowd-control until next round.
  • Mass Aegis (8) — allies within Tier squares gain +Tier to every defense this round.
  • Sanctum (9) — immune to one damage type for a round.
  • Mythic Stand (10) — invulnerable until the start of your next turn.

These were always the Bulwark's birthright; they no longer leak into everyone else's menu. Frame Dice and Ruin Charges endure as the strategic layer — Catastrophic Entry still sunders armor and breaches structures, Ruin still cuts a Siege's cost — and both refill on a Soma Break.

“Power is not rage. Power is what still obeys you after the world breaks.”

Archetype (Bad Eden): Violence (Warlord). Commander, breaker, disciplined engine of force. You do not merely hit hard — you make force coherent.

Archetype Effects

  • Faction Edge. This Archetype is associated with +10 Violence marks in faction calculus.
  • Tier Engine. See this Archetype’s Tier feats (Tier 1–4) for the full tactical and strategic expression of battlefield command, violent pressure, and military dominance.

attributes (Archetype ASI)

When you choose this Archetype, you gain 3 attribute points to distribute using the 2024 rules (no more than +2 to any one score). Common patterns include:

  • Iron Commander: +2 Violence, +1 Presence
  • Battlefield Mind: +2 Mind, +1 Violence
  • Frontline Tyrant: +1 Violence, +1 Body, +1 Presence

These are suggestions, not shackles. Any valid 3-point distribution is allowed.

description.value:
Occult Association (Bad Eden): Rosicrucian.

“I carry the old codes. I also carry a knife.”

Rosicrucians approach the Great Work like a courier network running through a burning city.

They preserve forbidden manuals, safeguard rituals, move people and knowledge between surviving nodes, and keep the chain of instruction alive when the world would prefer amnesia. Where some occult paths seek revelation or force, the Rosicrucian seeks continuity. The world cannot be repaired if the instructions are lost, the routes are severed, or the people who remember how to proceed are already dead.

To a Rosicrucian, the Great Work is not merely discovery. It is preservation, transit, and successful handoff.

How Rosicrucians pursue the Great Work:

  • By keeping archives, techniques, and living instruction intact
  • By building bridges between factions before they harden into wars
  • By turning safe passage into a strategic asset
  • By making recovered Sparks actually matter after recovery

Resonance: Netzach / Continuity — endurance, persistence, route-memory, and the stubborn Athletics of useful truth.

Tell-tales: precise manners, hidden caches, backup plans nested inside backup plans, and the calm confidence of someone who already mapped the exit.

Faction Effect (Passive):

  • +1 to Diplomacy marks rolls

Cost Principle: continuity creates obligation. Expect favors, route maintenance, political visibility, and pressure from everyone who now assumes your network will keep holding.

description.value:
Grim Persistence

You are difficult to kill because you do not stop.

Rules

Your Integrity maximum increases by an amount equal to twice your level. Additionally, once per Soma Break, when you are reduced to 0 Integrity but not killed outright, you may remain at 1 Integrity instead.

⚙ Integrity max +2 × level applies automatically; the hold-at-1 fires by itself, once per Soma Break.

Tier 4 — Rosicrucian

“When the Spark arrives, my people already have a place to put it.”

At Tier 4, your order stops feeling like a club and starts feeling like infrastructure. When your Domain achieves a Spark recovery, your network amplifies the downstream benefit.

Strategic (Faction Scale)

  • When your Domain successfully gathers a Spark of Light for the Great Work, increase the resulting Faction Resource Injection by 20%

The Great Work is not just discovery. It is what happens after discovery — and you are built for that.

Cost: once your network becomes the obvious place recovered value flows through, rivals, allies, and dependents all begin measuring you by whether that flow ever stops.

Difficult terrain is for people who pause.

Your movement speed cannot be reduced below half your base speed by any effect, condition, surface, or creature short of a physical barrier substantial enough to stop a charging rhino (GM call). This includes — but is not limited to — difficult terrain, grease, web, the restrained condition, the prone condition's stand-up cost, slowed/snared effects, and being grappled by a creature your size or smaller.

You still take damage from traps and hazardous terrain along your path; you simply do not stop for them. You may end movement voluntarily.

description.value:
Bad Eden Heritage (v1.1, RFI-native). Menhirkin heritage: Igneous.

“Some stone was born yelling.”

Menhirkin (Igneous). You are new rock. The Shattering was your birthday. The land that stood up and began answering chose you because it wanted a mouth that remembered being molten. You run hot, you cool slow, and you are, structurally, still furious about something.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Menhirkin).
  • Size. Medium.
  • Movement. 6 squares walking.
  • Lineage Lean. Menhirkin does not grant fixed attribute bonuses; your background handles increases. Your heritage leans toward Violence in fiction and through Tier powers.

Menhirkin Core: The Land Stood Up

Shared across all Menhirkin heritages. Granted at character creation via the base ancestry item.

  • Stone Soul. You count as Large for carry, shove, and grapple despite your Medium frame. You reroll the lowest die on checks to resist being forcibly moved.
  • Hex Recognition. Once per scene, while you are on a natural surface you are directly touching, you may whisper a single question about the place. The GM answers with one true thing the land knows.
  • Slow to Wear. You reroll the lowest die on Body checks against Stress, long-duration physical wear, forced marches, climate exposure, and sustained labor. You do not tire the way softer things tire.
  • Heavy Presence. Your weight and settledness are perceptible. Creatures within 2 squares of you know you are there even if they cannot see you; you roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on Intrigue (Stealth) checks unless you are on or in stone.

Igneous Traits

  • Heat Memory. When you take thermal damage with the fire flavor, you may bank that damage. Before your next Soma Break, you may spend the banked heat as a bonus action to add +1d10 exploding thermal damage (flavor: fire) to your next weapon attack, unarmed strike, or grapple that connects.
  • Molten Bearing. You count fire, smoke, ash, and heated terrain as normal ground for the purposes of difficult terrain and footing. Contact with your bare skin singes paper and warms metal.

Strategic Hooks (Foundry / Bad Eden)

  • Domain Edge. Your Domain gains +20 Violence marks and +10 Non-Lethal marks at campaign start.
  • Hex Synergy. In Volcanic / Thermal / Industrial-Furnace hexes, your Domain's heat-based or smelting operations cost 10 fewer marks (minimum 0).
  • Forge-Ready. Once per turn, your Domain may reroll one failed crafting or weapons-salvage check. The heat remembers the work.

Declare the line. The line happens.

The Breach — 1/scene (recovers on Soma Break). On your turn, declare a straight-line path to a destination within your maximum movement for the turn. You move to that destination, and any physical barrier in your way breaks open as you pass:

  • Wooden walls, doors, panes, and fortifications up to Hard hardness (DC 18) are broken open.

  • Stone walls and reinforced doors require a Violence attribute check vs Heroic DC 22 to pass through; on failure you stop adjacent to the barrier and lose the rest of the movement.

  • Any creature of size huge or smaller occupying a space along the line takes (Violence value + Bulwark Initiation) kinetic damage, (kinetic), and is knocked prone. They do not block your path.

You arrive upright, in your normal initiative slot, with whatever debris a person carries when they have just opened a wall.

Beauty - Balance that costs something. +1 Diplomacy, +1 Soft Power OPs

Tiphareth holds justice and mercy in living tension. It rewards balanced play, stability across multiple systems, and factions that survive by integrating contradictions instead of denying them.

Crew Type (Bad Eden): Covert Ops Cell.

“If you saw it happen, it wasn’t us.”

Covert Ops cells make wars quiet. They prefer locks to speeches, shadows to banners, and results to credit. They don’t start fights—they rearrange the board so the fight never happens.

  • Tactical Identity: You gain a skill rank in Stealth and with the Tinkering aptitude.
  • Strategic Identity: Your Domain starts with +1 Intrigue OPs.

Bladed Tempo

Your weapons are punctuation.

Rules

When you hit with a melee weapon attack, you may immediately draw or stow a weapon, or shift 1 square without provoking reaction strikes.

✍ Table rule.

description.value:
Decisive Momentum

You do not pause when the fight turns. You ride the turn.

Rules

When you reduce a hostile creature to 0 Integrity or land a critical hit, you may immediately move up to half your movement without provoking reaction strikes or make one weapon attack against a different creature within reach. You can use this principle once per round.

🃏 Card — once per round.

description.value:
⚙ ENGINE NOTE — Frame & Ruin are now ◆ Surge. Read Frame Die as banked Surge spent defensively, Ruin Charge as Surge spent offensively. Bulwarks bank +1 Surge when they take Integrity damage (max +2/round; +3 w/ Polarity Mastery on Mountain). Path kits live in the ◆ Surge menu. Automated: Polarity Mastery (melee strike, base die ≥ 8 → +1 Surge 1/round), Anchor or Advance + The Breach (clickable, 1/scene).

Movement is now a doctrine of the body.

While you have at least 1 Frame Die in your pool:

  • You are immune to forced movement, the staggered condition, and any effect that would stun, paralyze, or render you unconscious without first reducing your integrity to 0.

  • At the start of your turn you may spend any number of Frame Dice. For each one spent, roll the die and add the result to your movement speed (in feet) for that turn only.

  • You may pass through the space occupied by any creature or unattended object softer than reinforced stone (GM call) without stopping. You do not provoke reactions while doing so.

The world has two ways of saying no to change. You learn one of them today.

On gaining Bulwark Initiation 1 you receive:

  • Skill rank +1 in Athletics (Violence).

  • Skill rank +1 in one tool of your choice (any single tool tracked as a skill on your sheet).

  • Violence marks cap +3 and Siege marks cap +2 on your Domain.

  • Your Frame Dice pool comes online (persistence — d8 dice, spend to absorb hits or fuel doctrine effects). Pool max = max(2, ceil((Violence value + Bulwark Initiation) / 3)), capped at 8.

  • Your Ruin Charges pool comes online (inevitability — single-use charges, spend to fuel offensive doctrine effects). Same pool-size formula.

Both pools refill on a Soma Break. How you generate them depends on your chosen Path; see your doctrine's L1 feature.

"The land is not scenery. The land is a person. You are the version of it that finally stood up and walked over to complain."

You are not descended from the land. You are the land. A hex decided to become a person and the person is you. The standing stones on the ridge are distant cousins. The bedrock under the bunker is a grandparent. Mortals call you a Hex-Giant. You don't correct them.

Creature Type. Humanoid (Menhirkin). Size. Medium, but you count as Large for carrying capacity and the size of creatures you can shove or grapple. Speed. 6 squares

Heartstone (passive). A fragment of your home hex is literally inside you. While in any hex your Domain controls or has claimed: reroll the lowest die on Body checks (auto-fires), and you cannot be forcibly removed from the hex against your will (teleportation, banishment, forced march) without first being reduced to 0 Integrity.

Land Memory (1/Soma Break). Lay a hand on any surface older than you; the GM tells you one true thing the land remembers.

Living Rampart (1/Soma Break). Reaction — when a creature you can see targets an ally adjacent to you with an attack, the attacker rolls 3d10 keep lowest 2 on that attack roll.

Stonebound (passive). Reroll the lowest die on Body checks to resist being pushed, knocked Prone, or otherwise forcibly moved (auto-fires). Reroll the lowest die on Body checks to build, repair, or fortify structures, siegeworks, and defensive emplacements (auto-fires).

Strategic Hooks. Domain Edge: +20 Non-Lethal marks and +10 Violence marks at campaign start. Fortify Hex: first Patch the Breach or structure-repair Siege activity each Turn costs 10 fewer marks (min 0). Logistics Frame: 1/Turn, treat one raid/operation Logistics cost as Logistics −1 (min 0). Sentient Land (1/turn): consult the hex itself about a pending decision; one-sentence honest answer from the land's perspective.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Menhirkin: Hex-Giant Recovery: 3 active per-uses (2 Soma Break · 1 turn) + 2 reroll passives + Heartstone hex-protection  ·  Action: Picker (Land Memory · Living Rampart · Sentient Land · Heartstone)  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke. 4-slot picker — Land Memory (touch-the-old-stones), Living Rampart (ally-cover reaction), Sentient Land (1/turn faction question), Heartstone passive. Stonebound reroll grants auto-fire on Body checks for forced-movement and build/repair/fortify.

description.value:
Signature move. Once a scene, you choose which kind of inevitability you are.

Anchor or Advance — 1/scene (recovers on Soma Break). As part of any action on your turn, declare a stance. The chosen stance lasts until the end of your next turn:

  • Anchor. You cannot be moved against your will by any effect short of a Heroic-DC (22) push from a creature of your size or larger. Forced movement, knockback, teleportation targeting you, banishment, and dimensional swap effects all fail.

  • Advance. You cannot be prevented from reaching a destination you declare on the same action. Difficult terrain, conditions that halve speed, reaction strikes, and zone-of-control effects do not stop your movement toward that point. You may still take damage along the way.

Doctrine features at L5+ extend or modify which stance you favor.
